summary: Orphaned expense claim attachment truncation during upload blocking payrun
description:
Issue summary: Several employee expense claims uploaded on 2026-03-01 showed valid attachments in the UI but failed to map to expense lines during payrun generation. The payrun PR-2026-03-04-42 was blocked with 'attachment_type_unknown' errors and several claims were left in 'pending' state. Impact: Upcoming supplier reimbursements and corporate-card reimbursements for the March 4th payrun are delayed (~€37k total). Internal audit checklist demands attachments for reimbursements which increases manual workload until resolved.

Observed behavior: Attachments for ~12 claims are present in the employee profile but backend ingestion records show truncated filenames where the file extension was removed (e.g. 'receipt_12345' instead of 'receipt_12345.pdf'), causing the file-type sniffing routine to return 'unknown' and skip OCR/line extraction. This leaves the expense matcher unable to reconcile transaction lines, so claims are excluded from automated payrun inclusion.

Business impact: High — payrun blocked and finance must triage claims manually to avoid missing supplier deadlines.

Requested outcome: Identify root cause, apply temporary remediation to unblock the payrun (re-ingest or re-queue affected attachments), and implement a durable fix in the file-upload service to preserve extensions and validate content-type on ingest.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Employee uploads expense attachment via Expenses web UI (tested with Chrome 112 and Safari on macOS).
2) Attachment appears in UI with preview enabled.
3) Run internal ingestion job 'attachments-processor' or wait for scheduled ingestion window.
4) Verify DB record for attachment shows filename without extension and file_type = null.
5) Trigger payrun generation job; claim is skipped with 'attachment_type_unknown' and payrun enters 'blocked' state.
expected_result: Uploaded attachment retains filename and extension or has valid content-type recorded in the attachment metadata. Ingestion should process PDF/JPEG/PNG and OCR should extract lines so expense matcher can reconcile claims into payrun.
actual_result: Attachment metadata recorded with truncated filename (no extension) and file_type null. attachments-processor logs 'unable to determine mime type' and claim remains excluded from automated processing.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: INFO processing attachment id=att-9f8e size=142014
2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: WARN filename truncated detected: original='receipt_ÄÖ-12345.pdf' stored='receipt_ÄÖ-12345'
2026-03-01 09:12:07 attachments-processor: ERROR mime sniff returned empty for id=att-9f8e; skipping ocr

Hypothesis: UTF-8 characters in filename plus our legacy S3 key normalization is dropping trailing '.pdf' when names include non-ascii characters. Edge-case occurs when upload path length + normalized name crosses 120 bytes triggering substring operation that drops suffix.

Checked S3 object keys for affected files: keys exist and objects intact; object metadata 'Content-Type' is set to 'application/pdf' for some, but ingestion relies on database-stored filename for quick type decision — mismatch surfaced when filename lost extension.

Reproduced locally by uploading filename with surrogate characters via web UI and observing filename normalization routine in file-upload-service: url-encode -> utf8-normalize -> truncate(120) -> write. truncate(120) currently operates on bytes, not chars, causing suffix cut-off.

Temporary remediation applied: modified ingestion worker to fall back to S3 object's Content-Type header when filename does not contain extension. Re-queued affected attachments for processing (queue id: q-attachments-20260304-7).
Risk: Fallback increases processing latency but reduces manual interventions; permanent fix should be in upload service to avoid per-claim fallbacks.
logs: [attachments-processor] 2026-03-01T09:12:07Z id=att-9f8e ERROR unable to determine mime type from filename; attempting s3 metadata fallback
[payrun-generator] 2026-03-04T03:10:12Z warn claim c-78123 skipped reason='attachment_type_unknown' payrun=PR-2026-03-04-42
comments: Ava Kim (reporter) 2026-03-01: Filed after finance noticed 10+ claims missing OCR output during payrun prep. Attached sample affected claim IDs and screenshots in internal thread #finance-helpdesk.
Liam Patel (assignee) 2026-03-01: Acknowledge — triaging with SRE and platform eng. Will try re-queueing ingestion and test uploader truncation edge-cases.

SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-02: Confirmed truncation occurs when UTF-8 encoded filename bytes > 120. Created a sandbox test to repro. Recommended quick fix: attachments-processor should consult S3 Content-Type before skipping OCR.

Platform Eng (Meera Singh) 2026-03-03: Patch prepared to perform truncate by characters not bytes and to ensure suffix preservation. Raised PR #4882. Will coordinate Canary deploy to us-east then eu-west.
Finance Ops (Olivia Chen) 2026-03-04: Thanks — please prioritize fallback. We have payment windows on 2026-03-06. Manual processing for affected claims will add ~3 hours of workload if not automated.
workaround: 1) Re-queued affected attachments to attachments-processor with s3-metadata-fallback enabled (queue q-attachments-20260304-7). 2) Finance ops will accept payments for claims where OCR still fails via manual verification (guidance doc shared).
next_steps: Merge PR #4882 and deploy to file-upload-service with char-safe truncation and extension preservation.
Add automated test for non-ASCII filenames crossing the byte-length threshold.
Add monitoring alert: Ratio of attachments with null file_type > 0.5% for 15m should page Platform team.
Postmortem to document root cause and update expense ingestion runbook.
